Custom VJP rules that log or take gradient accumulators

Source: R/custom_derivatives.R
custom_vjp_defvjp_with_logs.Rd

Ports of custom_vjp.defvjp_with_logs and custom_vjp.defvjp_with_accums.

Usage

custom_vjp_defvjp_with_logs(
  f,
  fwd,
  bwd,
  symbolic_zeros = FALSE,
  optimize_remat = FALSE
)

custom_vjp_defvjp_with_accums(
  f,
  fwd,
  bwd,
  symbolic_zeros = FALSE,
  optimize_remat = FALSE
)

Arguments

f

A function created by custom_vjp().

fwd, bwd

Optional rules (can be set later with custom_vjp_defvjp()).

symbolic_zeros

Symbolic zeros mode (port of symbolic_zeros=True of custom_vjp.defvjp). The leaves of the arguments of fwd are then CustomVJPPrimal() records with elements value and perturbed (whether that argument is being differentiated), and the leaves of ct in bwd are SymbolicZero() objects where a cotangent is known to be zero. bwd may return SymbolicZero objects too.

optimize_remat

Run fwd through the remat_opt primitive (port of optimize_remat=True of custom_vjp.defvjp): values and derivatives are unchanged. jaxR keeps the forward computation whole (its dead code elimination has no rule that drops the primal part), so this saves no memory.

Value

A function with the custom VJP rule.

Details

With custom_vjp_defvjp_with_logs(), bwd returns a pair list(in_cts, logs): the usual cotangents and a named list of values to log out of the backward pass (or NULL). Apply the VJP function with its with_logs method to receive them: vjp_fun$with_logs(ct) returns list(arg_cts, logs). A plain call drops the logs. Log names must be unique within a backward pass.

With custom_vjp_defvjp_with_accums(), bwd(res, g, ...) receives one gradient accumulator per argument of the function (with the structure of the arguments, see ad_ValAccum) after its two usual arguments, pushes the cotangent contributions into them and returns NULL or a named list of logs.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
f <- custom_vjp(function(x, y) x * y)
f <- custom_vjp_defvjp_with_logs(f, function(x, y) list(x * y, list(x, y)),
  function(res, g) list(list(g * res[[2]], g * res[[1]]), list(g = g)))
vjp(f, 3, 4)[[2]]$with_logs(1)
} # }
